{{pagebanner|Batu Pahat banner.jpg}} [[File:BatuPahatRiver01.jpg|thumb|Batu Pahat]] '''Batu Pahat''', also called '''Bandar Penggaram''', is a town in Batu Pahat District, [[Johor]], [[Malaysia]]. ==Get in== === By car === Exit the North-South Expressway (PLUS) via Air Hitam/Yong Peng (if coming from the south) or Tangkak/Pagoh (if coming from the north) and follow the signs to Batu Pahat. Average journey times (via Expressway): * [[Kuala Lumpur]] (3.5 hours) * Johor Bahru (2 hours) * [[Singapore]] (2.5 hours) * [[KLIA]] (3 hours) === By train === There is no local train station. The nearest train station is in the nearby town of [[Kluang]]. === By plane === Batu Pahat does not have its own airport; the nearest airport is located in [[Malacca]] ({{IATA|MKZ}}), and has very limited connections. For most visitors, the nearest airports of significance are the ones in [[Kuala Lumpur]] ({{IATA|KUL}}), [[Johor Bahru]] ({{IATA|JHB}}) and [[Singapore]] ({{IATA|SIN}}). ==Get around== {{mapframe|1.85|102.96|zoom=12}} === By car === The best way to get around is by car or taxi. There are several one-way roads so be wary and keep a look out for the roadsigns. === By bus === The main local bus terminal is in the town centre next to the intercity bus terminal. Stage buses take you to the surrounding suburbs and are fairly cheap. ==See== [[File:Penggaram Square.JPG|thumb|Penggaram Square]] *Check out the famous Batu Pahat roundabout with the 100-year-old tree. * {{see | name=Batu Pahat Stadium | alt=Stadium Batu Pahat | url= | email= | address=Kampung Bahagia | lat=1.844743 | long=102.933418 | directions= | phone= | tollfree= | hours= | price= | image=Batu Pahat Stadium.JPG | wikidata=Q94494052 | lastedit=2018-03-30 | content=Stadium }} * {{see | name=Penggaram Square | alt=Dataran Penggaram | url= | email= | address=Jalan Rahmat, Kampung Bahagia | lat=1.846740 | long=102.934481 | directions= | phone= | tollfree= | hours= | price=Free | image=Penggaram Square.JPG | wikidata=Q64997312 | lastedit=2018-03-30 | content=Public square }} * {{see | name=Tasik Y Recreational Park | alt=Taman Rekreasi Tasik Y | url= | email= | address=Jalan Sejati | lat=1.842999 | long=102.936742 | directions=Take BP-001 bus from Batu Pahat Terminal and alight at the park | phone= | tollfree= | hours= | price= | image=Taman Rekreasi Tasik Y, Batu Pahat, Johor. Look for these Malay specialities: * Pisang goreng - only the original fried banana in batter along Jalan Omar (Warung Tandan Emas). Its unique taste comes from being mixed with their delicious blend of kicap pedas (spicy soy sauce). * Nasi bariani - seen all around Malaysia, the nasi bariani Batu Pahat originates from here. There are plentiful shops around Batu Pahat selling them but the best allegedly is located across the Batu Pahat Bridge opposite Putra Hospital. Alas, commercialisation has caused its quality to deteriorate. There are a few coffee shops selling delicious teatime cakes, toasts, half-boiled eggs and desserts. ===Budget=== * {{eat | name=Ah See Wan Tan Mee | alt= | url= | email= | address=2, Jalan Jenang Dalam | lat=1.8504367 | long= 102.9273405 | directions= | phone= | tollfree= | fax= | hours= | price= | lastedit=2022-08-01 | content=Chinese food is very famous among the locals.
